title: Indicated Renewal Premium on the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy
content:
**Rule.** When a LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy renewal is offered, the indicated renewal premium for the upcoming term is the expiring term premium increased by the tier's inflation guard percentage and then by the rating percentage, rounded half-up to the cent once, on the final figure. The standard rating percentage is zero.

## The definition in parts

- The expiring term premium is the annual premium of the term now in force.
- Increasing by a percentage means multiplying by one hundred plus that percentage and dividing by one hundred.
- The inflation guard increase comes first; the rating percentage then acts on the premium already increased by the inflation guard.
- No figure is rounded along the way; the single rounding, half-up to the cent, is on the indicated renewal premium itself.
- With the rating percentage at zero, the indicated renewal premium is the expiring term premium increased by the inflation guard percentage.

## Worked figures (hypothetical policies)

| Expiring term premium (USD) | Inflation guard taken as | After the inflation guard | Rating percentage | Indicated renewal premium (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,850.00 | 4 percent | 1,924.00 | 0 | 1,924.00 |
| 1,233.33 | 5 percent | 1,294.9965 | 0 | 1,295.00 |
| 980.00 | 0 percent | 980.00 | 0 | 980.00 |

The second row shows the single rounding: 1,233.33 multiplied by 105 and divided by 100 is 1,294.9965, which rounds half-up to 1,295.00 only at the end.
